pr_title: Completion field to support multiple completion multi-fields
pr_body:
The completion field supports multi-fields. In case the sub-field is another completion field, the whole object structure from the incoming document needs to provided as input to the sub-field while parsing it. We have a special XContentParser for this scenario, but it does not handle returning the same object structure multiple times. That is why you can have only one completion sub-field within a completion field, and the error returned when such mechanism breaks is a general parsing error (that mentions a field called dummy_field) that makes users think they have done something wrong in their document.

This commit expands testing for this scenario and extends the parser to support it.

As part of this change, a new parser is created for each sub-field, which makes it possible to expose the same object structure multiple times, for instance in case a completion field has more than one completion sub-fields.

Additionally, the wrapping of both the geo_point multi field parser and the completion multi field parser into a dummy_field object is removed in favour of returning the correct `currentName` of the main field we are parsing.

Additionally getTokenLocation is tweaked to return the location of the field we are parsing in the document, so that error messages become clearer when things go wrong.

Closes #83534
pr_comments: Hi @javanna, I've created a changelog YAML for you.

issue_context.title: Completion field can't hold more than one completion multi-field

review_comments: I don't know if this last section should be a TODO . It feels like this parser grew out of control and I find the whole mechanism counter-intuitive. Maybe instead of faking parsing this way we should consider using a map to pass around the content to multi-fields, or creating a new parser each time instead of reusing the same parser to read the same values/object .
Passing a Map was what we did before and it caused problems of its own.  I like the idea of creating a new parser for each multifield though, that feels a lot cleaner.
It should be possible to create a new parser for each multi-field, I am working on a follow-up that should allow to remove some of this complexity. Do you mind if we merge this one in the meantime?

with the recent changes, two out of three problems that I listed are solved. The fact that the parser is delicate stays, as it changes behaviour depending on what consumers do, but I think I can accept that given that it's the only one that does this.

I have removed the wrapping, I am not sure why it was needed. We do have the problem now that currentName at the top-level is null hence if something breaks during parsing, users get an error with a null field name, whereas they would get an error about dummy_field before. I don't see other places where the top-level field could be used.

On the other hand, if there are errors while parsing the document they happen mostly when parsing the parent field, and multi-field parsing should go smooth unless we have bugs.
there's a single user of this left, hence I moved it to a private method local to where it's still needed.

what's the plan here? From the code, it does not seem like we can phase out geohash given it's what any geopoint sub-field reads. I believe the comment is inaccurate as also keyword and text will get the geohash.
